quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (CFO Roger Dassen): total net sales were a record EUR 11.7 billion, towards the high end of guidance, reflecting strong execution of the capacity ramp. Net system sales EUR 8.4 billion: EUR 4.1 billion EUV system sales (including the sale of one High-NA EUV system) and EUR 4.3 billion non-EUV system sales; system sales split logic 54% / memory 46%. Installed Base Management sales EUR 3.3 billion, exceeding guidance by almost EUR 0.4 billion, primarily on strong demand for productivity upgrade products in both EUV and Deep UV. Gross margin 57.5%, above guidance, primarily on very high-margin components within the installed base business; Q3 was a record for both total net sales and gross margin. R&D around EUR 1.2 billion and SG&A around EUR 0.4 billion (as guided); effective tax rate 16.1%. Net income EUR 5 billion (42.5% of total net sales), including around EUR 0.5 billion from an increase in the valuation of ASML's initial investment in Mistral AI; EPS EUR 12.95. Free cash flow EUR 11.4 billion, underpinned by customers' strong order momentum and the related down payments; cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments EUR 12.7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: total net sales EUR 11.7 billion (record); EUV EUR 4.1 billion (one High-NA); non-EUV EUR 4.3 billion; installed base EUR 3.3 billion; gross margin 57.5%; EPS EUR 12.95; free cash flow EUR 11.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO): Q4 2026 total net sales between EUR 14.2 billion and EUR 15.2 billion with a gross margin of around 57%, installed base management sales around EUR 3.7 billion, R&D around EUR 1.2 billion and SG&A around EUR 0.4 billion; the Q4 gross margin is a little lower than Q3 mainly because ramp costs for the capacity increases partly offset the higher-volume fixed-cost coverage. FY2026 total net sales between EUR 44 billion and EUR 45 billion with a gross margin of around 56% — an anticipated year-over-year increase of around 36%, reflecting over 45% growth in EUV, around 20% growth in non-EUV system sales and around 50% growth in installed base management sales. By end use, logic net system sales to grow around 10% (the advanced logic piece expected to grow over 25%) and memory net system sales around 75%. China still expected at around 20% of total net sales this year; FY2026 annualized effective tax rate around 17%. Management expects the business to continue to accelerate in Q4 against very strong customer demand for all products and services.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 net sales between EUR 14.2 billion and EUR 15.2 billion, gross margin around 57%; FY2026 between EUR 44 billion and EUR 45 billion, gross margin around 56%, around 36% growth; EUV over 45%; installed base around 50%; logic around 10%, memory around 75%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (CFO Roger Dassen / CEO Christophe Fouquet): ASML anticipates output of roughly 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026, nearly 50% more than the 44 systems shipped last year; for Deep UV immersion, where the initial output target was well below the prior year, it now expects to deliver a similar quantity in 2026 as in 2025. Last quarter's plan was +30% capacity in 2027 for both low-NA EUV and DUV immersion and to investigate a further 30% in 2028, but ASML now anticipates its current planned output in 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand, and is looking into expanding 2028 capacity even above the 30% year-on-year growth target for both low-NA EUV and immersion. CEO: no new 2027 or 2028 numbers ('far too early'); extra opportunity is easier to enable mostly in 2028 than in the shorter term. Levers named by the CEO: using more of the existing footprint for output (low-NA EUV and Deep UV), shortening factory cycle time as the NXE:3800E matures and dropping qualification steps agreed with customers, and the supply chain — the main supplier challenge is making sure suppliers can go up 30% every year (EUV went up 50% this year), ASML keeps adding suppliers for non-critical parts, and every number shared has been validated against the supply chain. CFO: ramp costs are incurred both at ASML and in the supply chain, where 'in some places, there is some help needed'. Productivity upgrades on the installed base add wafer capacity on the same footprint.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026 vs 44 last year (nearly 50% more); 2027 capacity +30%; 2028 capacity above the 30% year-on-year growth target

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and visibility (CEO Christophe Fouquet / CFO Roger Dassen): order momentum continues to build as customers shift focus beyond 2027 — ASML is increasingly receiving orders for 2028, and customers are expressing interest in placing orders for 2029 and even 2030. CFO: those 2029-2030 POs have not yet been accepted; ASML first wants to mirror the total demand customers signal for 2029-2030 against its expected capacity, so it does not accept orders from some customers and then tell another long-standing customer 'Sorry, we're sold out'. The interest 'is not linked to one specific customer' and is 'far broader'. An ASML order carries a down payment 'enough to hurt' and getting out of it 'comes at a price, not just the down payment'; non-current liabilities include down payments and are a lagging proxy for order intake, as ASML gives no PO numbers. CEO: the demand is validated against customers' detailed fab construction plans and is 'real and not inflated by any potential buying behavior'; customer clean-room readiness is only a tactical constraint (a system may slip from one quarter to the next) and not a major factor on demand, while the CFO said customers must execute the 2027-2028 construction diligently so it does not become one.
quarterly_data.figure: orders increasingly for 2028; customer interest in orders for 2029 and 2030 (not yet accepted)

quarterly_data.signal: Demand environment (CEO Christophe Fouquet): the pace of the AI build-out continues to be very robust; supply shortages across advanced logic and memory nodes 'continue to increase in size and in time horizon', and customers' demand signals strengthened through the quarter. Leading-edge high-volume customers have very good visibility from the growing number of long-term commitments they are securing with their own customers and have concluded that demand for their products will outpace supply through at least 2028, so they are accelerating capacity build-out plans and preparing for further expansion beyond 2028 — for ASML, greater short-term demand across the whole holistic lithography portfolio and improved longer-term visibility, especially for EUV. CEO: memory and logic are 'very much coupled' in delivering AI capacity, and logic demand is also very strong.
quarterly_data.figure: customers see demand outpacing supply through at least 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing (CFO Roger Dassen / CEO Christophe Fouquet): the price-increase conversations with customers begun in July are completed and led to price increases on the most critical products — the high-range, high-volume manufacturing products that bring the most value; upgrade prices, closely tied to tool prices, will follow the same pattern. No impact on 2026; some positive effect in the course of 2027 on revenue, ASPs and gross margin, with the full, sustained impact from 2028 onwards. Part of the increase covers the extraordinary ramp, including in the supply chain, but 'a significant part of it is directly accretive to the gross margin'. Not planned as an annual event: the CFO said ASML 'would not be looking at repeating this every year' and stays with value-based pricing so it never has to negotiate price decreases in a downturn; the CEO called it one of the very first such discussions, with 'a clear acceptance that maybe the overall value in the ecosystem is shifting', triggered by AI to some extent. CEO: the move of all immersion versions to 330 wafers per hour is also a value, margin and pricing opportunity, as value scales with throughput as for EUV.
quarterly_data.figure: price increases on most critical products: no 2026 impact, some in 2027, full from 2028

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 gross-margin drivers (CFO Roger Dassen; a 2027 percentage will be given in January 2027): positives are volume (the 30% increase, if ramp costs are controlled, gives better fixed-cost coverage), mix (low-NA EUV and immersion, while dry business also keeps increasing), the price increase, and a better EUV mix as this year's D models mostly drop out next year and 'a few Fs' come in. To watch: ramp costs for 2027 and beyond, and the upgrade business as 'an important swing factor' — upgrades are very strong this year, many installed tools are not yet upgraded, and ASML will bring new upgrade products that open a new installed-base market. CFO: memory comes close to logic in 2027, but 'logic will outweigh memory in the total book of business for next year'; CEO: the logic-memory ratio will most probably increase towards memory.

New systems (CFO Roger Dassen / CEO Christophe Fouquet): ASML plans to introduce its next-generation low-NA EUV system, the NXE:3800F, starting in small quantities at the beginning of 2027, specified at 260 wafers per hour versus the 230 wafers per hour capability of the NXE:3800E. It also plans to introduce the next-generation critical Deep UV immersion system running at 330 wafers per hour; the CEO said all immersion versions will go to 330 wafers per hour to the beginning of next year, a short-term action to add capacity. These products add incremental wafer capacity as they ramp in the coming years.
quarterly_data.figure: NXE:3800F 260 wafers per hour from the beginning of 2027 (vs 230 wafers per hour NXE:3800E); immersion 330 wafers per hour

quarterly_data.signal: Metrology (CEO Christophe Fouquet): in Q3 ASML shipped the first YieldStar 550 metrology system, an overlay measurement system designed for the tighter process control of the 14 angstrom node in logic and the 1D node in DRAM, delivering more than 60% greater productivity than the previous-generation YieldStar. YieldStar demand is expected to more than double for the coming years versus 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: first YieldStar 550 shipped; more than 60% greater productivity; demand to more than double vs 2025

quarterly_data.signal: High-NA EUV (CEO Christophe Fouquet): meaningful momentum this quarter, with industry announcements showing progress from development towards production; Samsung announced plans to introduce High-NA EUV into high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Availability across the existing High-NA EUV fleet is approaching 90%, and ASML now expects adoption to increase node by node. In Q&A: 'we're still looking at the very initial ramps'; customers will need more tools every year as they validate High-NA in manufacturing and plan more layers, and 'the number will grow for sure year after year', though the big capacity ramp can affect the High-NA rollout positively or negatively depending on whether customers see it as added capacity or a slowdown. Customers' wide participation in the 12-inch photomask consortium signals more High-NA adoption over time, and ASML sees potentially new customers on High-NA as well.
quarterly_data.figure: High-NA fleet availability approaching 90%; Samsung High-NA EUV high-volume manufacturing in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: China (CFO Roger Dassen / CEO Christophe Fouquet): intrinsic demand in China is strong — mainstream logic and memory for domestic consumption, with many fabs coming online; China is 20% this year and the CFO said that for 2027 and beyond the demand situation in China remains very strong. CEO: Chinese customers 'all want to work with us'; ASML gives no market-share number but it is 'extremely high, especially on immersion'; as long as market access is preserved, the likelihood of major competition in China is still pretty low, and progress on a Chinese competing tool 'is not very strong'. The EUV DRAM demand discussed for 2029-2030 excludes China.

contracts.signal: CEO Christophe Fouquet: Intel announced that it has exposed more than 1 million wafers using its High-NA EUV systems, with performance that meets or exceeds comparable layers patterned using low-NA EUV — cited as evidence of High-NA EUV progressing from development towards production.

contracts.signal: CEO Christophe Fouquet: TSMC announced plans to introduce High-NA EUV into high-volume manufacturing in 2030. ASML, in collaboration with TSMC, began an industry-wide initiative to develop larger-format EUV photomasks, aiming to establish a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031 and enter production in 2033; the CEO called TSMC's drive on the 12-inch critical mask a signal that customers expect more and more use of High-NA.

quarterly_data.signal: Memory / DRAM (CFO Roger Dassen / CEO Christophe Fouquet): memory was 46% of Q3 net system sales. The CFO said the FY2026 memory growth is driven by customers' capacity expansion and the increasing adoption of EUV on advanced DRAM nodes; the CEO said the memory increase is 'mostly DRAM', the result of 'this huge memory investment'. ASML continues to see new customers on low-NA EUV, especially in DRAM, which 'go a bit beyond the T customer' (not named), and a similar trend on High-NA. On 2029-2030 order interest: equal interest and demand trajectory from DRAM and logic customers, with DRAM 'a bit more aggressive on the buildup of those capacity'; this EUV discussion excludes China.
quarterly_data.figure: memory 46% of Q3 net system sales
